critical_issues.msg: Path '/api/v1/sales/leads' will resolve to /api/v1/customers/api/v1/sales/leads due to the router's prefix='/api/v1/customers'
critical_issues.suggestion: Change to path='/sales/leads' so the full path becomes /api/v1/customers/sales/leads

critical_issues.msg: Path '/api/v1/sales/leads/recycle' also doubles the prefix for the same reason
critical_issues.suggestion: Change to path='/sales/leads/recycle' so the full path becomes /api/v1/customers/sales/leads/recycle

critical_issues.msg: get_leads_by_owner is called with positional args in wrong order; plan specifies (owner_id, tenant_id, page, page_size) but CustomerService method signature is (tenant_id, owner_id, page, page_size)
critical_issues.suggestion: Swap to: await service.get_leads_by_owner(ctx.tenant_id, ctx.user_id, page=page, page_size=page_size)

critical_issues.msg: session parameter lacks type annotation — violates router pattern convention (session: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)).

Creates a duplicate, competing declarative Base — engine.py declares `Base = declarative_base()` separately from db.base.Base, so ORM models using db.base.Base are invisible to engine.py's Base during autogenerate migrations.
critical_issues.suggestion: Import Base from db.base instead of from internal.db.engine, or consolidate to a single Base in db.base and import it from there.

critical_issues.msg: Hardcoded Supabase pooler IP '13.114.6.6' has no runtime fallback — if SUPABASE_POOLER_HOST is unset in production, the hardcoded IP is used silently without validation.
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove the default IP from the fallback; require SUPABASE_POOLER_HOST to be explicitly set, or fail with a clear error if neither is configured.

critical_issues.msg: src/models/customer.py and src/db/models/customer.py define two separate, incompatible Customer representations — the dataclass lacks tenant_id and all ORM-specific fields (created_at server_default, indexed tenant_id), so a Customer from the service layer is a different shape than CustomerModel from the DB layer.
critical_issues.suggestion: Consolidate to a single Customer representation: either use the dataclass as a Pydantic-free plain-Python object and make db/models/customer.py use it via `from models.customer import Customer`, or use Pydantic BaseModel as the canonical type across service and router layers.

critical_issues.msg: Rule 27/48: model_post_init raising ValueError instead of Pydantic ValidationError circumvents the standard error handling flow and produces an opaque 500 instead of a structured 422 at the API boundary.
critical_issues.suggestion: Use a Pydantic field_validator on 'field' to raise a proper ValidationError: @field_validator('field') def check_field(cls, v): raise ValueError(...) from pydantic.

critical_issues.msg: Rule 46: verify_token() never reads from the revoked_tokens table — revoked tokens are still treated as valid because the revocation check is write-only.
critical_issues.suggestion: Add a DB lookup in verify_token or in the middleware that calls it: check that the token's jti does not exist in revoked_tokens before returning the payload.

critical_issues.msg: Rule 123: create_customer uses flush() + refresh() in a service, which the project rules say fights the router-owned transaction lifecycle and corrupts the unit of work.
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove the flush() before refresh(); let the router layer own the commit/flush cycle. Keep only flush() when auto-generated IDs are needed by subsequent operations (e.g. auto_assign_lead), then remove refresh() and return the object.

critical_issues.msg: Rule 31/39: bulk_recycle issues one UPDATE per lead in a loop (N queries); should use a single batched UPDATE statement.
critical_issues.suggestion: Use a single UPDATE with a WHERE id IN (...) clause and a SQL array-append expression for recycle_history.

critical_issues.msg: Rule 53 / Rule 25: `check_and_recycle_leads` calls `notif_svc.send_lead_recycled()` which does not exist on `NotificationService` — the method name is `send_notification()` — so every notification call will raise `AttributeError`, silently swallowed by the bare `except Exception: pass` on line 421.
critical_issues.suggestion: Replace `notif_svc.send_lead_recycled(cust_id, prev_owner)` with the correct API: `notif_svc.send_notification(user_id=prev_owner, notification_type='lead_recycled', title='Lead Recycled', content=f'Lead {cust_id} has been recycled', tenant_id=tid)`, or implement `send_lead_recycled` on `NotificationService`.

suggestions.msg: Step 3 mentions Redis for round-robin cursor but Redis is not mentioned anywhere in CLAUDE.md or project dependencies
suggestions.suggestion: Clarify whether Redis is a new dependency or if the cursor should be stored in the database instead (e.g. TenantModel or a dedicated cursor table)

suggestions.msg: Step 5 references RBACService.require_permission but the service may not exist or may have a different API in the current codebase
suggestions.suggestion: Verify RBACService.exists() and its exact API before writing the router authorization layer

suggestions.msg: Step 6 path GET /api/v1/sales/leads will double-prefix /api/v1 since customers_router already has prefix=/api/v1/customers
suggestions.suggestion: Change path to just /sales/leads so it resolves correctly to /api/v1/customers/sales/leads; same fix needed for POST /api/v1/sales/leads/recycle → /sales/leads/recycle

suggestions.msg: Step 8 describes calling auto_assign_lead from create_customer but does not specify how LeadRoutingService gets a session when called from within a service method
suggestions.suggestion: Clarify whether LeadRoutingService is instantiated with the session passed in, or if the router layer should be responsible for triggering auto-assignment after create_customer returns

suggestions.msg: asyncio is imported but only used in run_async_migrations; the offline path run_migrations_offline does not use it
suggestions.suggestion: Remove unused import: delete line 2 `import asyncio`

suggestions.msg: lead_routing_router is imported and exported but src/api/routers/lead_routing.py may not exist yet (per issue-77 plan it is listed as a new file)
suggestions.suggestion: Confirm src/api/routers/lead_routing.py exists and is complete before this __init__ is deployed; if the file is missing the module will fail to import at startup

suggestions.msg: total = len(items) counts in-memory after a full table scan rather than a SQL COUNT; for large recycled-lead sets this is inefficient and unreliable
suggestions.suggestion: Replace with a separate COUNT query: count_result = await session.execute(select(func.count()).where(...same filters...)); total = count_result.scalar_one()

suggestions.msg: session type annotation is missing AsyncSession — should be `session: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)` for consistency and mypy
suggestions.suggestion: Add `from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession` to imports and annotate session parameter

suggestions.msg: owner_id=0 means unassigned; checking `if customer.owner_id` misses the case where owner_id is 0 (falsy but valid) but the else branch runs when it shouldn't
suggestions.suggestion: Change to `if customer.owner_id is not None and customer.owner_id > 0:` to correctly differentiate 0 from NULL

suggestions.msg: Lines 139, 158, 169, 181, 191, 203, 215, 227, 239, 250, 270, 324, 361, 374, 391 all use `session=Depends(get_db)` without type annotation — inconsistent with project convention
suggestions.suggestion: Add `session: AsyncSession` type annotation to all session parameters

suggestions.msg: PaginationQuery class is defined but never used — dead code
suggestions.suggestion: Remove PaginationQuery if not used, or use it in list_customers to replace inline Query defaults

suggestions.msg: N+1 query pattern: loop issues one UPDATE per rule_id instead of batching into a single statement.
suggestions.suggestion: Batch into one UPDATE with CASE WHEN id = rid THEN val ELSE priority END, or use core insert(...).values(list_of_dicts) on the model table.

suggestions.msg: _require_admin_or_manager has an unused session parameter; all callers pass it but it is never used.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove session parameter: async def _require_admin_or_manager(ctx: AuthContext) -> None

suggestions.msg: TOCTOU race: rule.is_active is read then a separate UPDATE uses not rule.is_active; concurrent toggle can be lost.
suggestions.suggestion: Use UPDATE ... SET is_active = NOT is_active (inline expression) so the DB computes the new value atomically, removing the need to read-then-write.

suggestions.msg: RolePermissionModel is imported and included in __all__ but RolePermissionModel is not listed — stale __all__ after a model was added.
suggestions.suggestion: Add 'RolePermissionModel' to __all__ list.

suggestions.msg: Imports at module level load all ORM models eagerly; for large projects this can slow startup and increase memory use.
suggestions.suggestion: Consider lazy imports (import inside functions) for rarely-used models to defer loading.

suggestions.msg: Mapped[list] is an unparameterized generic — should specify contained type for type-checker accuracy.
suggestions.suggestion: Use Mapped[list[dict]] for tags and recycle_history.

suggestions.msg: owner_id defaults to 0 (Python-side) rather than server_default; functionally equivalent but inconsistent with other column defaults that use server_default.
suggestions.suggestion: Align with server_default or use a server_default for consistency.

suggestions.msg: Commented-out index definition left in __table_args__; dead commented code should be removed.
suggestions.suggestion: Delete the commented index block entirely.

suggestions.msg: Mapped[list] is an unparameterized generic — should specify contained type (list[dict]) since conditions_json stores structured rule conditions.
suggestions.suggestion: Use Mapped[list[dict]] for conditions_json.

suggestions.msg: Exports `create_engine_from_env` and `get_engine` (sync-only functions) from an async-first module, sending a confusing signal that sync DB access is part of the active stack.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove sync-only functions from this module's public API, or document clearly that they are legacy/script-only.

suggestions.msg: The entire internal/db/ package is dead code — all routers import `get_db` from db.connection and the lifespan in main.py calls functions from db.connection, so none of these exports are used.
suggestions.suggestion: Delete src/internal/db/ entirely, or wire it up as the canonical path and remove the equivalent code from db.connection to eliminate duplication.

suggestions.msg: Uses module-level global variables for engine and session factory singletons with double-checked locking — works but is fragile; a race during module load could cause issues under gunicorn/uvicorn workers.
suggestions.suggestion: Use a class or function-local singleton pattern with proper lock semantics, or document that this module must be imported once at startup before any concurrent access.

suggestions.msg: `load_dotenv()` called at module level runs as a side-effect at import time, making environment loading order-dependent and harder to reason about.
suggestions.suggestion: Call load_dotenv() explicitly in the app entry point (main.py) or in the settings module rather than at the bottom of an infrastructure module.

suggestions.msg: Lifespan imports `ensure_engine` and `dispose_engine` from `db.connection` but `get_db_session` (also from db.connection) is never used — only `get_db` FastAPI dependency is used by routers, so the session scope function is dead code.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove `get_db_session` from db.connection if it's no longer needed, or use it consistently across the codebase.

suggestions.msg: Health check endpoint '/ ' returns a static success response without verifying DB connectivity, so it cannot distinguish a healthy service from one with a broken DB pool.
suggestions.suggestion: Add a lightweight DB ping (e.g. `await session.execute(text('SELECT 1'))`) or at least note in the response that this is a liveness check, not a readiness check.

suggestions.msg: Generic exception handler logs `type(exc).__name__` and `str(exc)` but omits stack trace, making production debugging significantly harder.
suggestions.suggestion: Add `exc_info=True` to the logger.error call: `logger.error(..., exc_info=True)` so the full traceback is captured.

suggestions.msg: `owner_id` defaults to 0 if missing in `from_dict`, silently producing an invalid owner rather than raising a validation error.
suggestions.suggestion: Raise a ValidationException if owner_id is missing or not a positive integer, rather than defaulting to 0.

suggestions.msg: `datetime.now(UTC)` in a field default_factory captures time at class-definition time rather than at instance creation for the same field in from_dict (which calls it at call-time), producing inconsistent behaviour between the two constructors.
suggestions.suggestion: Use `field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(UTC))` explicitly, or document that callers should always pass explicit created_at/updated_at.

suggestions.msg: to_dict() duplicates Pydantic's built-in model_dump(); callers can use that directly.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove to_dict() and have callers use data.model_dump() instead.

suggestions.msg: from_dict() bypasses Pydantic validation by manually extracting fields; invalid inputs silently get None defaults instead of surfacing errors.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove from_dict() and call CustomerCreateDTO(**data) directly; let Pydantic handle validation.

suggestions.msg: owner_id defaults to 0 (int) rather than None; 0 is an unlikely valid FK but is indistinguishable from 'unset' in the DTO layer.
suggestions.suggestion: Use owner_id: int | None = None for clarity.

suggestions.msg: SUPPORTED_FIELDS is a module-level mutable set; while not dangerous here, it's a shared global that could be accidentally modified at runtime.
suggestions.suggestion: Use frozenset for SUPPORTED_FIELDS.

suggestions.msg: Rule 26/28: import os inside __init__ shadows the module-level import and makes dependency on environment implicit and harder to test.
suggestions.suggestion: Pass secret_key explicitly at construction time from the caller; remove the in-function import.

suggestions.msg: Rule 53/29: sanitize_string strips '--' which mangles legitimate user input (e.g. math content); SQLAlchemy ORM prevents injection so the sanitization is unnecessary and harmful.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove sanitize_string or restrict it to plain-text display contexts only, not storage.

suggestions.msg: Rule 28: self.session is guaranteed non-None by __init__ signature; the 'if not self.session' guard is dead code.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the 'if not self.session: return True' branch.

suggestions.msg: is_valid_email uses a regex match when pydantic's EmailStr could handle validation declaratively; keep the helper only if needed outside Pydantic contexts.
suggestions.suggestion: Use pydantic.EmailStr or EmailStr from pydantic-email-validators instead of a manual regex.

suggestions.msg: Rule 31: add_tag fetches the full row then modifies tags in Python; should use a single UPDATE statement for atomicity.
suggestions.suggestion: Replace get + modify + flush + refresh with an UPDATE that appends to the tags JSON array using PostgreSQL array_append.

suggestions.msg: Rule 31: bulk_import loops over customers calling session.add per item instead of using session.add_all for a single flush.
suggestions.suggestion: Use session.add_all(customers) before the single flush() call.

suggestions.msg: Rule 41: bulk_recycle updates rows without setting updated_at, making the last modification time stale.
suggestions.suggestion: Add updated_at=now to the .values() call inside the loop.

suggestions.msg: Redundant double negation: `assigned_at.is_(None).is_(False)` is equivalent to `assigned_at.isnot(None)`, i.e. `assigned_at IS NOT NULL` — the extra `.is_(False)` adds nothing.
suggestions.suggestion: Replace with `CustomerModel.assigned_at.is_(None)` — SQLAlchemy's `is_()` returns a binary boolean, calling `is_(False)` on it is a no-op; the intent is already correct, just clean it up.

suggestions.msg: Rule 119: `team` assignee_type branch is implemented as a no-op comment — all active users of the tenant are selected, which is semantically wrong for team-scoped routing (should filter to team members only).
suggestions.suggestion: Either implement the team filter (e.g. join on a team_members table keyed by `assignee_id`) or remove the elif branch and fall through to round-robin explicitly with a comment.

suggestions.msg: Rule 19: Magic number `20` is hardcoded as the default `max_load_per_rep` — the same value is used as the hardcoded fallback in `_get_max_load_per_rep`, making it implicit rather than declared.
suggestions.suggestion: Extract to a module-level constant `DEFAULT_MAX_LOAD_PER_REP = 20` and reference it in both places.

suggestions.msg: Rule 46: Silent exception swallowing — `except Exception: pass` hides `AttributeError` (from the missing method above), `OperationalError`, and any other failure in the notification path with no logging or retry.
suggestions.suggestion: Log the exception at WARNING level and re-raise if it is non-recoverable. At minimum: `import logging; logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` then `except Exception as e: logger.warning('notification failed for tenant %s: %s', tid, e)`.

suggestions.msg: Rule 28: Module-level `_tenant_id_web` and `_tenant_id_2_web` globals are mutable state shared across tests — they retain their values between test runs when the module is reloaded, causing tenant-ID bleed across test files.
suggestions.suggestion: Replace the global pattern with a pytest `session` or `module` scoped fixture that returns the same value within a session but resets between sessions. For example: move the cache into a `@pytest.fixture(scope='session')` fixture that stores state in its own closure.

suggestions.msg: Rule 15 / 20: `AsyncGenerator` is imported twice — once at line 27 (`from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator`) and again at line 297 (`from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator`). The second import is redundant.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the duplicate import at line 297.

suggestions.msg: Rule 51: `JWT_SECRET_KEY` is hardcoded as a string literal `'integration-test-jwt-secret-key'`. While this is in a test file, it violates the principle of not hardcoding secrets and could leak if test output is logged.
suggestions.suggestion: Use `os.environ.get("JWT_SECRET_KEY")` with a clearly-prefixed test-only environment variable (e.g. `TEST_JWT_SECRET_KEY`) sourced from `os.environ` or a `.env.test` file.

suggestions.msg: Rule 64: `test_reassign_lead_logs_history` asserts `recycle_count == 1` and `len(recycle_history) == 1` — but the test customer is created via `create_customer` which (Step 8 of that method) calls `auto_assign_lead` for leads with `owner_id=0`. Here the customer starts with `owner_id=1`, so auto-assignment is not triggered, but this implicit coupling is fragile.
suggestions.suggestion: Add an explicit comment explaining why the test is immune to Step 8 auto-assignment, or restructure to use a direct insert to make the intent unambiguous.

suggestions.msg: Rule 64 / 65: `test_bulk_recycle` calls `cust_svc.create_customer` for leads that already have `owner_id=uid` — Step 8 of `create_customer` triggers `auto_assign_lead`, but since `owner_id != 0` it does not trigger. However `bulk_recycle` filters to `owner_id != 0`, so a lead with a real owner should be recycled. This test relies on implicit non-auto-assignment behavior.
suggestions.suggestion: Add a comment at the top of the test noting that leads with `owner_id != 0` skip the auto-assignment Step 8 guard, making `create_customer` safe to use here.

suggestions.msg: Rule 63 / 68: The comment at line 160 acknowledges that `get_unassigned_leads` depends on `create_customer` behavior — the test works around it by inserting directly. This is correct but should be a fixture helper rather than inline SQL to reduce duplication.
suggestions.suggestion: Extract the direct-insert pattern to a `_seed_unassigned_lead` helper in conftest.py so multiple tests can reuse it.

suggestions.msg: Rule 28 / 29: `make_routing_rule_handler` uses `if not hasattr(state, 'routing_rules')` to lazily initialize shared state on a `MockState` instance — this couples the handler to implementation details of `MockState` and makes stateful test behavior non-obvious.
suggestions.suggestion: Initialize `routing_rules` and `routing_rules_next_id` explicitly in `MockState.__init__` so the handler can assume they exist without `hasattr` checks.

suggestions.msg: Rule 18: `MockRow.__getattr__` raises `AttributeError` for any attribute not in the mapping, but silently swallows the request for `'_mapping'` (raises because it starts with `_`) — this is correct behavior but the interaction between `__getattr__` and private-name check is subtle.
suggestions.suggestion: Add a short docstring to `__getattr__` explaining the `_`-prefix guard and the fallthrough behavior.

suggestions.msg: Rule 65: `make_mock_session` returns a fully-stitched `MagicMock` with `execute = AsyncMock` but `add`, `delete`, `flush` etc. as `MagicMock` (non-async). If a service accidentally calls `await session.add(...)` it will fail at runtime but not in tests, creating a false pass.
suggestions.suggestion: Make `add`, `delete`, `flush`, `refresh`, `commit`, `rollback`, `close` also `AsyncMock` so async usage is tested faithfully. `MagicMock` is only correct for sync methods like `session.get`.

suggestions.msg: Global autouse patch on auto_assign_lead applies to every test in the file — violates rule 67 (mocking not excessive) and contradicts the per-test mock ownership convention in CLAUDE.md.
suggestions.suggestion: Move the patch into the specific test that needs it as a local fixture, or remove it if auto_assign_lead is intentionally not tested in this file.

suggestions.msg: Comment on line 158 references rule numbers (121/122) but test code should not contain comment-based rule citations.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the inline rule-number comment; the convention is documented in CLAUDE.md, not in the test.

suggestions.msg: Same comment pattern as line 158, repeated here.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the inline rule-number comment from line 187.

suggestions.msg: Clean schema-validation unit tests with no issues.

TestConditionOperator class (lines 119-129) duplicates exact test coverage already present in test_lead_routing_router.py: operators EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, IN, NOT_IN, GT, LT, GTE, LTE, BETWEEN are tested identically in both files — violates rule 110 (no copy-paste duplication across modules).
suggestions.suggestion: Remove TestConditionOperator class from test_lead_routing_service.py; it already imports from the same module and the enum value tests belong in the router test file.

suggestions.msg: TestRuleCondition class (lines 136-149) duplicates test_rejects_unsupported_field, test_accepts_supported_fields, and test_all_operators_work — identical logic already exists in test_lead_routing_router.py (lines 20-32) — violates rule 110.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove TestRuleCondition class from test_lead_routing_service.py; RuleCondition schema validation belongs in the dedicated schema test file.

warnings.msg: TOCTOU race: rule.is_active is read then a separate UPDATE uses not rule.is_active; concurrent toggle can be lost.
warnings.suggestion: Use UPDATE ... SET is_active = NOT is_active (inline expression) so the DB computes the new value atomically, removing the need to read-then-write.

warnings.msg: RolePermissionModel is imported and included in __all__ but RolePermissionModel is not listed — stale __all__ after a model was added.
warnings.suggestion: Add 'RolePermissionModel' to __all__ list.

warnings.msg: Imports at module level load all ORM models eagerly; for large projects this can slow startup and increase memory use.
warnings.suggestion: Consider lazy imports (import inside functions) for rarely-used models to defer loading.

warnings.msg: Mapped[list] is an unparameterized generic — should specify contained type for type-checker accuracy.
warnings.suggestion: Use Mapped[list[dict]] for tags and recycle_history.

warnings.msg: owner_id defaults to 0 (Python-side) rather than server_default; functionally equivalent but inconsistent with other column defaults that use server_default.
warnings.suggestion: Align with server_default or use a server_default for consistency.

warnings.msg: Commented-out index definition left in __table_args__; dead commented code should be removed.
warnings.suggestion: Delete the commented index block entirely.

warnings.msg: Mapped[list] is an unparameterized generic — should specify contained type (list[dict]) since conditions_json stores structured rule conditions.
warnings.suggestion: Use Mapped[list[dict]] for conditions_json.

warnings.msg: Exports `create_engine_from_env` and `get_engine` (sync-only functions) from an async-first module, sending a confusing signal that sync DB access is part of the active stack.
warnings.suggestion: Remove sync-only functions from this module's public API, or document clearly that they are legacy/script-only.

warnings.msg: The entire internal/db/ package is dead code — all routers import `get_db` from db.connection and the lifespan in main.py calls functions from db.connection, so none of these exports are used.
warnings.suggestion: Delete src/internal/db/ entirely, or wire it up as the canonical path and remove the equivalent code from db.connection to eliminate duplication.

warnings.msg: Uses module-level global variables for engine and session factory singletons with double-checked locking — works but is fragile; a race during module load could cause issues under gunicorn/uvicorn workers.
warnings.suggestion: Use a class or function-local singleton pattern with proper lock semantics, or document that this module must be imported once at startup before any concurrent access.

warnings.msg: `load_dotenv()` called at module level runs as a side-effect at import time, making environment loading order-dependent and harder to reason about.
warnings.suggestion: Call load_dotenv() explicitly in the app entry point (main.py) or in the settings module rather than at the bottom of an infrastructure module.

warnings.msg: Lifespan imports `ensure_engine` and `dispose_engine` from `db.connection` but `get_db_session` (also from db.connection) is never used — only `get_db` FastAPI dependency is used by routers, so the session scope function is dead code.
warnings.suggestion: Remove `get_db_session` from db.connection if it's no longer needed, or use it consistently across the codebase.

warnings.msg: Health check endpoint '/ ' returns a static success response without verifying DB connectivity, so it cannot distinguish a healthy service from one with a broken DB pool.
warnings.suggestion: Add a lightweight DB ping (e.g. `await session.execute(text('SELECT 1'))`) or at least note in the response that this is a liveness check, not a readiness check.

warnings.msg: Generic exception handler logs `type(exc).__name__` and `str(exc)` but omits stack trace, making production debugging significantly harder.
warnings.suggestion: Add `exc_info=True` to the logger.error call: `logger.error(..., exc_info=True)` so the full traceback is captured.

warnings.msg: `owner_id` defaults to 0 if missing in `from_dict`, silently producing an invalid owner rather than raising a validation error.
warnings.suggestion: Raise a ValidationException if owner_id is missing or not a positive integer, rather than defaulting to 0.

warnings.msg: `datetime.now(UTC)` in a field default_factory captures time at class-definition time rather than at instance creation for the same field in from_dict (which calls it at call-time), producing inconsistent behaviour between the two constructors.
warnings.suggestion: Use `field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(UTC))` explicitly, or document that callers should always pass explicit created_at/updated_at.

warnings.msg: to_dict() duplicates Pydantic's built-in model_dump(); callers can use that directly.
warnings.suggestion: Remove to_dict() and have callers use data.model_dump() instead.

warnings.msg: from_dict() bypasses Pydantic validation by manually extracting fields; invalid inputs silently get None defaults instead of surfacing errors.
warnings.suggestion: Remove from_dict() and call CustomerCreateDTO(**data) directly; let Pydantic handle validation.

warnings.msg: owner_id defaults to 0 (int) rather than None; 0 is an unlikely valid FK but is indistinguishable from 'unset' in the DTO layer.
warnings.suggestion: Use owner_id: int | None = None for clarity.

warnings.msg: SUPPORTED_FIELDS is a module-level mutable set; while not dangerous here, it's a shared global that could be accidentally modified at runtime.
warnings.suggestion: Use frozenset for SUPPORTED_FIELDS.

warnings.msg: Rule 26/28: import os inside __init__ shadows the module-level import and makes dependency on environment implicit and harder to test.
warnings.suggestion: Pass secret_key explicitly at construction time from the caller; remove the in-function import.

warnings.msg: Rule 53/29: sanitize_string strips '--' which mangles legitimate user input (e.g. math content); SQLAlchemy ORM prevents injection so the sanitization is unnecessary and harmful.
warnings.suggestion: Remove sanitize_string or restrict it to plain-text display contexts only, not storage.

warnings.msg: Rule 28: self.session is guaranteed non-None by __init__ signature; the 'if not self.session' guard is dead code.
warnings.suggestion: Remove the 'if not self.session: return True' branch.

warnings.msg: is_valid_email uses a regex match when pydantic's EmailStr could handle validation declaratively; keep the helper only if needed outside Pydantic contexts.
warnings.suggestion: Use pydantic.EmailStr or EmailStr from pydantic-email-validators instead of a manual regex.

warnings.msg: Rule 31: add_tag fetches the full row then modifies tags in Python; should use a single UPDATE statement for atomicity.
warnings.suggestion: Replace get + modify + flush + refresh with an UPDATE that appends to the tags JSON array using PostgreSQL array_append.

warnings.msg: Rule 31: bulk_import loops over customers calling session.add per item instead of using session.add_all for a single flush.
warnings.suggestion: Use session.add_all(customers) before the single flush() call.

warnings.msg: Rule 41: bulk_recycle updates rows without setting updated_at, making the last modification time stale.
warnings.suggestion: Add updated_at=now to the .values() call inside the loop.

warnings.msg: Redundant double negation: `assigned_at.is_(None).is_(False)` is equivalent to `assigned_at.isnot(None)`, i.e. `assigned_at IS NOT NULL` — the extra `.is_(False)` adds nothing.
warnings.suggestion: Replace with `CustomerModel.assigned_at.is_(None)` — SQLAlchemy's `is_()` returns a binary boolean, calling `is_(False)` on it is a no-op; the intent is already correct, just clean it up.

warnings.msg: Rule 119: `team` assignee_type branch is implemented as a no-op comment — all active users of the tenant are selected, which is semantically wrong for team-scoped routing (should filter to team members only).
warnings.suggestion: Either implement the team filter (e.g. join on a team_members table keyed by `assignee_id`) or remove the elif branch and fall through to round-robin explicitly with a comment.

warnings.msg: Rule 19: Magic number `20` is hardcoded as the default `max_load_per_rep` — the same value is used as the hardcoded fallback in `_get_max_load_per_rep`, making it implicit rather than declared.
warnings.suggestion: Extract to a module-level constant `DEFAULT_MAX_LOAD_PER_REP = 20` and reference it in both places.

warnings.msg: Rule 46: Silent exception swallowing — `except Exception: pass` hides `AttributeError` (from the missing method above), `OperationalError`, and any other failure in the notification path with no logging or retry.
warnings.suggestion: Log the exception at WARNING level and re-raise if it is non-recoverable. At minimum: `import logging; logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` then `except Exception as e: logger.warning('notification failed for tenant %s: %s', tid, e)`.

warnings.msg: Rule 28: Module-level `_tenant_id_web` and `_tenant_id_2_web` globals are mutable state shared across tests — they retain their values between test runs when the module is reloaded, causing tenant-ID bleed across test files.
warnings.suggestion: Replace the global pattern with a pytest `session` or `module` scoped fixture that returns the same value within a session but resets between sessions. For example: move the cache into a `@pytest.fixture(scope='session')` fixture that stores state in its own closure.

warnings.msg: Rule 15 / 20: `AsyncGenerator` is imported twice — once at line 27 (`from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator`) and again at line 297 (`from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator`). The second import is redundant.
warnings.suggestion: Remove the duplicate import at line 297.

warnings.msg: Rule 51: `JWT_SECRET_KEY` is hardcoded as a string literal `'integration-test-jwt-secret-key'`. While this is in a test file, it violates the principle of not hardcoding secrets and could leak if test output is logged.
warnings.suggestion: Use `os.environ.get("JWT_SECRET_KEY")` with a clearly-prefixed test-only environment variable (e.g. `TEST_JWT_SECRET_KEY`) sourced from `os.environ` or a `.env.test` file.

warnings.msg: Rule 64: `test_reassign_lead_logs_history` asserts `recycle_count == 1` and `len(recycle_history) == 1` — but the test customer is created via `create_customer` which (Step 8 of that method) calls `auto_assign_lead` for leads with `owner_id=0`. Here the customer starts with `owner_id=1`, so auto-assignment is not triggered, but this implicit coupling is fragile.
warnings.suggestion: Add an explicit comment explaining why the test is immune to Step 8 auto-assignment, or restructure to use a direct insert to make the intent unambiguous.

warnings.msg: Rule 64 / 65: `test_bulk_recycle` calls `cust_svc.create_customer` for leads that already have `owner_id=uid` — Step 8 of `create_customer` triggers `auto_assign_lead`, but since `owner_id != 0` it does not trigger. However `bulk_recycle` filters to `owner_id != 0`, so a lead with a real owner should be recycled. This test relies on implicit non-auto-assignment behavior.
warnings.suggestion: Add a comment at the top of the test noting that leads with `owner_id != 0` skip the auto-assignment Step 8 guard, making `create_customer` safe to use here.

warnings.msg: Rule 63 / 68: The comment at line 160 acknowledges that `get_unassigned_leads` depends on `create_customer` behavior — the test works around it by inserting directly. This is correct but should be a fixture helper rather than inline SQL to reduce duplication.
warnings.suggestion: Extract the direct-insert pattern to a `_seed_unassigned_lead` helper in conftest.py so multiple tests can reuse it.

warnings.msg: Rule 28 / 29: `make_routing_rule_handler` uses `if not hasattr(state, 'routing_rules')` to lazily initialize shared state on a `MockState` instance — this couples the handler to implementation details of `MockState` and makes stateful test behavior non-obvious.
warnings.suggestion: Initialize `routing_rules` and `routing_rules_next_id` explicitly in `MockState.__init__` so the handler can assume they exist without `hasattr` checks.

warnings.msg: Rule 18: `MockRow.__getattr__` raises `AttributeError` for any attribute not in the mapping, but silently swallows the request for `'_mapping'` (raises because it starts with `_`) — this is correct behavior but the interaction between `__getattr__` and private-name check is subtle.
warnings.suggestion: Add a short docstring to `__getattr__` explaining the `_`-prefix guard and the fallthrough behavior.

warnings.msg: Rule 65: `make_mock_session` returns a fully-stitched `MagicMock` with `execute = AsyncMock` but `add`, `delete`, `flush` etc. as `MagicMock` (non-async). If a service accidentally calls `await session.add(...)` it will fail at runtime but not in tests, creating a false pass.
warnings.suggestion: Make `add`, `delete`, `flush`, `refresh`, `commit`, `rollback`, `close` also `AsyncMock` so async usage is tested faithfully. `MagicMock` is only correct for sync methods like `session.get`.

warnings.msg: Global autouse patch on auto_assign_lead applies to every test in the file — violates rule 67 (mocking not excessive) and contradicts the per-test mock ownership convention in CLAUDE.md.
warnings.suggestion: Move the patch into the specific test that needs it as a local fixture, or remove it if auto_assign_lead is intentionally not tested in this file.

warnings.msg: Comment on line 158 references rule numbers (121/122) but test code should not contain comment-based rule citations.
warnings.suggestion: Remove the inline rule-number comment; the convention is documented in CLAUDE.md, not in the test.

warnings.msg: Same comment pattern as line 158, repeated here.
warnings.suggestion: Remove the inline rule-number comment from line 187.

warnings.msg: Clean schema-validation unit tests with no issues.

TestConditionOperator class (lines 119-129) duplicates exact test coverage already present in test_lead_routing_router.py: operators EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, IN, NOT_IN, GT, LT, GTE, LTE, BETWEEN are tested identically in both files — violates rule 110 (no copy-paste duplication across modules).
warnings.suggestion: Remove TestConditionOperator class from test_lead_routing_service.py; it already imports from the same module and the enum value tests belong in the router test file.

warnings.msg: TestRuleCondition class (lines 136-149) duplicates test_rejects_unsupported_field, test_accepts_supported_fields, and test_all_operators_work — identical logic already exists in test_lead_routing_router.py (lines 20-32) — violates rule 110.

issues.suggestion: Pass secret_key explicitly at construction time from the caller; remove the in-function import.

issues.message: Rule 53/29: sanitize_string strips '--' which mangles legitimate user input (e.g. math content); SQLAlchemy ORM prevents injection so the sanitization is unnecessary and harmful.
issues.suggestion: Remove sanitize_string or restrict it to plain-text display contexts only, not storage.

issues.message: Rule 46: verify_token() never reads from the revoked_tokens table — revoked tokens are still treated as valid because the revocation check is write-only.
issues.suggestion: Add a DB lookup in verify_token or in the middleware that calls it: check that the token's jti does not exist in revoked_tokens before returning the payload.

issues.message: Rule 28: self.session is guaranteed non-None by __init__ signature; the 'if not self.session' guard is dead code.
issues.suggestion: Remove the 'if not self.session: return True' branch.

issues.message: is_valid_email uses a regex match when pydantic's EmailStr could handle validation declaratively; keep the helper only if needed outside Pydantic contexts.
issues.suggestion: Use pydantic.EmailStr or EmailStr from pydantic-email-validators instead of a manual regex.

parsed.summary: Token revocation is write-only (revoked tokens still verify); in-function import and dead session guard add noise; sanitize_string is unnecessary and destructive.

issues.message: Rule 123: create_customer uses flush() + refresh() in a service, which the project rules say fights the router-owned transaction lifecycle and corrupts the unit of work.
issues.suggestion: Remove the flush() before refresh(); let the router layer own the commit/flush cycle. Keep only flush() when auto-generated IDs are needed by subsequent operations (e.g. auto_assign_lead), then remove refresh() and return the object.

issues.message: Rule 31: add_tag fetches the full row then modifies tags in Python; should use a single UPDATE statement for atomicity.
issues.suggestion: Replace get + modify + flush + refresh with an UPDATE that appends to the tags JSON array using PostgreSQL array_append.

issues.message: Rule 31/39: bulk_recycle issues one UPDATE per lead in a loop (N queries); should use a single batched UPDATE statement.
issues.suggestion: Use a single UPDATE with a WHERE id IN (...) clause and a SQL array-append expression for recycle_history.

issues.message: Rule 31: bulk_import loops over customers calling session.add per item instead of using session.add_all for a single flush.
issues.suggestion: Use session.add_all(customers) before the single flush() call.

issues.message: Rule 41: bulk_recycle updates rows without setting updated_at, making the last modification time stale.
issues.suggestion: Add updated_at=now to the .values() call inside the loop.

parsed.summary: Multiple flush()+refresh() patterns violating transaction rules; bulk operations issue N individual queries instead of batched statements.

issues.message: Redundant double negation: `assigned_at.is_(None).is_(False)` is equivalent to `assigned_at.isnot(None)`, i.e. `assigned_at IS NOT NULL` — the extra `.is_(False)` adds nothing.
issues.suggestion: Replace with `CustomerModel.assigned_at.is_(None)` — SQLAlchemy's `is_()` returns a binary boolean, calling `is_(False)` on it is a no-op; the intent is already correct, just clean it up.

issues.message: Rule 119: `team` assignee_type branch is implemented as a no-op comment — all active users of the tenant are selected, which is semantically wrong for team-scoped routing (should filter to team members only).
issues.suggestion: Either implement the team filter (e.g. join on a team_members table keyed by `assignee_id`) or remove the elif branch and fall through to round-robin explicitly with a comment.

issues.message: Rule 19: Magic number `20` is hardcoded as the default `max_load_per_rep` — the same value is used as the hardcoded fallback in `_get_max_load_per_rep`, making it implicit rather than declared.
issues.suggestion: Extract to a module-level constant `DEFAULT_MAX_LOAD_PER_REP = 20` and reference it in both places.

issues.message: Rule 53 / Rule 25: `check_and_recycle_leads` calls `notif_svc.send_lead_recycled()` which does not exist on `NotificationService` — the method name is `send_notification()` — so every notification call will raise `AttributeError`, silently swallowed by the bare `except Exception: pass` on line 421.
issues.suggestion: Replace `notif_svc.send_lead_recycled(cust_id, prev_owner)` with the correct API: `notif_svc.send_notification(user_id=prev_owner, notification_type='lead_recycled', title='Lead Recycled', content=f'Lead {cust_id} has been recycled', tenant_id=tid)`, or implement `send_lead_recycled` on `NotificationService`.

issues.message: Rule 46: Silent exception swallowing — `except Exception: pass` hides `AttributeError` (from the missing method above), `OperationalError`, and any other failure in the notification path with no logging or retry.
issues.suggestion: Log the exception at WARNING level and re-raise if it is non-recoverable. At minimum: `import logging; logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` then `except Exception as e: logger.warning('notification failed for tenant %s: %s', tid, e)`.

parsed.summary: Core routing engine is sound, but has one critical bug (missing `send_lead_recycled` method + bare `except`), a no-op team branch, a redundant double-negation IS NULL check, and a hardcoded magic number.

issues.message: Rule 28: Module-level `_tenant_id_web` and `_tenant_id_2_web` globals are mutable state shared across tests — they retain their values between test runs when the module is reloaded, causing tenant-ID bleed across test files.
issues.suggestion: Replace the global pattern with a pytest `session` or `module` scoped fixture that returns the same value within a session but resets between sessions. For example: move the cache into a `@pytest.fixture(scope='session')` fixture that stores state in its own closure.

issues.message: Rule 15 / 20: `AsyncGenerator` is imported twice — once at line 27 (`from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator`) and again at line 297 (`from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator`). The second import is redundant.
issues.suggestion: Remove the duplicate import at line 297.

issues.message: Rule 51: `JWT_SECRET_KEY` is hardcoded as a string literal `'integration-test-jwt-secret-key'`. While this is in a test file, it violates the principle of not hardcoding secrets and could leak if test output is logged.
issues.suggestion: Use `os.environ.get("JWT_SECRET_KEY")` with a clearly-prefixed test-only environment variable (e.g. `TEST_JWT_SECRET_KEY`) sourced from `os.environ` or a `.env.test` file.

parsed.summary: Integration conftest is well-structured with proper NullPool and Pgbouncer workarounds, but uses module-level mutable globals for tenant IDs and has a duplicate import.

issues.message: Rule 64: `test_reassign_lead_logs_history` asserts `recycle_count == 1` and `len(recycle_history) == 1` — but the test customer is created via `create_customer` which (Step 8 of that method) calls `auto_assign_lead` for leads with `owner_id=0`. Here the customer starts with `owner_id=1`, so auto-assignment is not triggered, but this implicit coupling is fragile.
issues.suggestion: Add an explicit comment explaining why the test is immune to Step 8 auto-assignment, or restructure to use a direct insert to make the intent unambiguous.

issues.message: Rule 64 / 65: `test_bulk_recycle` calls `cust_svc.create_customer` for leads that already have `owner_id=uid` — Step 8 of `create_customer` triggers `auto_assign_lead`, but since `owner_id != 0` it does not trigger. However `bulk_recycle` filters to `owner_id != 0`, so a lead with a real owner should be recycled. This test relies on implicit non-auto-assignment behavior.
issues.suggestion: Add a comment at the top of the test noting that leads with `owner_id != 0` skip the auto-assignment Step 8 guard, making `create_customer` safe to use here.

issues.message: Rule 63 / 68: The comment at line 160 acknowledges that `get_unassigned_leads` depends on `create_customer` behavior — the test works around it by inserting directly. This is correct but should be a fixture helper rather than inline SQL to reduce duplication.
issues.suggestion: Extract the direct-insert pattern to a `_seed_unassigned_lead` helper in conftest.py so multiple tests can reuse it.

parsed.summary: Integration tests correctly use the real DB via fixtures and cover good scenarios, but several tests carry implicit assumptions about `create_customer` Step 8 auto-assignment behavior that deserve explicit comments or fixture extraction.

issues.message: Rule 28 / 29: `make_routing_rule_handler` uses `if not hasattr(state, 'routing_rules')` to lazily initialize shared state on a `MockState` instance — this couples the handler to implementation details of `MockState` and makes stateful test behavior non-obvious.
issues.suggestion: Initialize `routing_rules` and `routing_rules_next_id` explicitly in `MockState.__init__` so the handler can assume they exist without `hasattr` checks.

issues.message: Rule 18: `MockRow.__getattr__` raises `AttributeError` for any attribute not in the mapping, but silently swallows the request for `'_mapping'` (raises because it starts with `_`) — this is correct behavior but the interaction between `__getattr__` and private-name check is subtle.
issues.suggestion: Add a short docstring to `__getattr__` explaining the `_`-prefix guard and the fallthrough behavior.

issues.message: Rule 65: `make_mock_session` returns a fully-stitched `MagicMock` with `execute = AsyncMock` but `add`, `delete`, `flush` etc. as `MagicMock` (non-async). If a service accidentally calls `await session.add(...)` it will fail at runtime but not in tests, creating a false pass.
issues.suggestion: Make `add`, `delete`, `flush`, `refresh`, `commit`, `rollback`, `close` also `AsyncMock` so async usage is tested faithfully. `MagicMock` is only correct for sync methods like `session.get`.

parsed.summary: Unit conftest provides a comprehensive mock SQL layer, but `make_routing_rule_handler` uses fragile `hasattr` checks and several session methods are sync MagicMock when they should be AsyncMock for accurate test coverage.

issues.message: Global autouse patch on auto_assign_lead applies to every test in the file — violates rule 67 (mocking not excessive) and contradicts the per-test mock ownership convention in CLAUDE.md.
issues.suggestion: Move the patch into the specific test that needs it as a local fixture, or remove it if auto_assign_lead is intentionally not tested in this file.

issues.message: Comment on line 158 references rule numbers (121/122) but test code should not contain comment-based rule citations.
issues.suggestion: Remove the inline rule-number comment; the convention is documented in CLAUDE.md, not in the test.

issues.message: Same comment pattern as line 158, repeated here.
issues.suggestion: Remove the inline rule-number comment from line 187.

parsed.summary: Custom mock_db_session fixture works correctly but a global autouse patch on auto_assign_lead applies to all tests and inline rule-number comments add noise.
Clean schema-validation unit tests with no issues.

issues.message: TestConditionOperator class (lines 119-129) duplicates exact test coverage already present in test_lead_routing_router.py: operators EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, IN, NOT_IN, GT, LT, GTE, LTE, BETWEEN are tested identically in both files — violates rule 110 (no copy-paste duplication across modules).
issues.suggestion: Remove TestConditionOperator class from test_lead_routing_service.py; it already imports from the same module and the enum value tests belong in the router test file.

issues.message: TestRuleCondition class (lines 136-149) duplicates test_rejects_unsupported_field, test_accepts_supported_fields, and test_all_operators_work — identical logic already exists in test_lead_routing_router.py (lines 20-32) — violates rule 110.
issues.suggestion: Remove TestRuleCondition class from test_lead_routing_service.py; RuleCondition schema validation belongs in the dedicated schema test file.

parsed.summary: Well-structured unit tests for evaluate_conditions and get_sla_status, but TestConditionOperator and TestRuleCondition duplicate coverage already present in test_lead_routing_router.py.
